note: Scanner install catalog for `commitwork setup` (bin/setup.mjs). Per tool: a short `why`, one package id per supported manager (brew = macOS/Linux, winget/scoop = Windows, pipx = anywhere Python is), and a `url` fallback printed when no manager is available or an install fails. `manual: true` tools are checked and reported but never auto-installed. brew ids verified 2026-07-24; winget/scoop ids are from each project's install docs and are re-probed after install, so a stale id degrades to the url fallback rather than a silent failure. SEVEN TOOLS WERE ADDED 2026-09-02 (bandit, brakeman, bundle-audit, elixir, mix, hlint, phpcs) after a census found eight tools declared in security-baseline.json requires.tools and absent from here — cargo-audit was the one already listed. `commitwork setup` could therefore never install them, and their lanes skipped forever with `n/a — tool:x`, which reads exactly like correct language gating. bin/test/install-catalog-covers-manifest.test.mjs now fails if the two files disagree. overwatch-layer-spine WAS ADDED 2026-09-04: not a scanner, but the one catalogued thing that is configuration rather than a binary — its `steps` are keyed by the check ids admin/lib/spine-preconditions.mjs reports, so the Overwatch tab can name the exact step that is absent WINDOWS PASS 2026-09-04. Two entry SHAPES exist and bin/setup.mjs implemented only one: brew/winget/scoop/pipx/npm carry a PACKAGE ID, while cargo/gem/composer/go carry a WHOLE COMMAND STRING. The command-string managers were declared here and absent from setup.mjs's MANAGERS table, so they were INERT — cargo-audit, brakeman, bundle-audit, psalm and phpcs-security-audit have no other installer and therefore printed 'no installer for this platform' on EVERY platform, including a Windows box with cargo on PATH. An entry no manager can act on is worse than a missing one: the missing one is a gap somebody can see. `providedBy` (mix<-elixir, cargo-clippy<-cargo) was likewise unread. Four ids were added in this pass and each was VERIFIED ON THE BOX rather than copied from docs: zizmor.zizmor and GolangCI.golangci-lint resolve in `winget search`; the two `go install` lines were RUN, and both binaries now resolve on PATH. Nothing was added that could not be checked — opengrep and sobelow stay uninstallable and are now REPORTED as a catalog gap of ours rather than as a platform limitation.

cargo-audit.why: RustSec advisories for resolved Cargo graphs (deps-rust-audit second-opinion lane)

gitleaks.why: fast filesystem secret scan + pre-commit hook

betterleaks.why: second secret-scan engine with confidence and live validation

pipx.why: Python application installer; nine scanners (semgrep among them) install through it, and on Linux without Homebrew it is the manager that unblocks the most

gem.why: RubyGems, which brakeman and bundler-audit install through; arrives with Ruby

bwrap.why: bubblewrap, the Linux host sandbox every lane runs inside; without it each lane runs unconfined and records isolation none

pasta.why: pasta (package passt), the user-mode network for Linux lanes with egress: it gives each one its own network namespace with the internet and no host loopback. Without it those lanes are refused and record noscan

go.why: Go toolchain — required by gosec and govulncheck. A toolchain OLDER than a repo's `go` directive cannot load its module graph, so both scanners fail open rather than reporting

gosec.why: Go SAST — the Go lane the codeql checks (js-ts, java) do not cover

govulncheck.why: Go dependency + stdlib vulns WITH reachability — the only lane that can say an advisory is present but unreached

opengrep.why: OSS fork of Semgrep, kept as a standby engine. Same rule YAML, same p/ registry packs, same SARIF — so a licensing change costs a binary swap rather than a rewrite. No Homebrew formula: download the signed release asset and VERIFY IT, do not pipe an installer to a shell. `cosign verify-blob --certificate opengrep_osx_arm64.cert --signature opengrep_osx_arm64.sig --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/opengrep/opengrep/.*' --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com <binary>` returns Verified OK for v1.26.0.

actionlint.why: GitHub Actions workflow correctness + inline-run shellcheck. Catches the untrusted-input script-injection sink that zizmor's posture audit and semgrep's source rules both leave to the workflow layer.

shellcheck.why: shell correctness + injection lint for CI steps, install scripts and hooks. Run with --format=json1, never --format=json: the bare array the latter emits makes a clean run and a run that examined nothing byte-identical.

codeql.why: deep SAST. The CLI alone cannot analyse: `database analyze` needs QUERY PACKS, downloaded separately and PER LANGUAGE — a pack list that lags the lane list fails at analyze time, after the database has already built.

ready.why: the binary resolves but `database analyze` aborts with "Query pack codeql/<lang>-queries cannot be found" — measured 0 passes / 27 noscans across a fleet sweep while the CLI was on PATH the whole time. The readiness probe asks for PYTHON deliberately: it is the pack most recently added to the lane set, so it is the one a stale postInstall will be missing.

act.why: run real workflow YAML locally (--act checks)

osv-scanner.why: OSV dependency scan without the Docker detour

nuclei.why: templated DAST against live targets (runtime manifest)

testssl.sh.why: TLS/cipher audit of live endpoints (runtime manifest)

docker.why: daemon for osv-scanner (docker path), deps-updates, dast

guarddog.why: supply-chain metadata heuristics over the resolved npm tree (typosquats, deceptive authors, hijackable maintainer domains) — Apache-2.0, no account, no token. OPTIONAL: supply-chain-guarddog runs the ghcr.io/datadog/guarddog image via docker, so the native CLI is only needed for per-package deep source analysis (`guarddog npm scan <pkg>`), which verify cannot do

safe-chain.why: INSTALL-TIME gate (Aikido Safe Chain, tokenless, no build data shared): proxies npm/yarn/pnpm/bun and pip/uv/poetry installs and blocks known-malicious packages BEFORE the tarball is fetched. Not a scanner and not a commitwork check — the sweep never installs, so nothing here can cover the moment a postinstall script actually executes. Install it on developer machines; in CI use the --ci flag (PATH shims instead of shell aliases)

bandit.why: Python SAST (sast-python-bandit) — AST-level checks for the Python idioms that become vulnerabilities

brakeman.why: Rails-aware SAST (sast-ruby-brakeman) — routes/controllers/views, not generic pattern rules
brakeman.postInstall: needs Ruby >= 3.2. macOS system Ruby is 2.6, where gem silently installs brakeman 5.4.1 instead of failing — install brew ruby first, and symlink the gem bin into the brew prefix, which brew does not do for gems.

bundle-audit.why: ruby-advisory-db lookups for a resolved Gemfile.lock (deps-ruby-bundler-audit)

elixir.why: Erlang/Elixir runtime the sobelow ESCRIPT runs on, and the mix that installs it — the sast-elixir-sobelow lane invokes sobelow directly, never a mix task

mix.why: Elixir build tool the sobelow lane runs through — SHIPPED WITH elixir, never installed on its own

bearer.why: data-flow/PII SAST across JS, Ruby, Java, PHP, Python, Go (sast-bearer)
bearer.postInstall: third-party tap: `brew tap bearer/tap` then `brew trust bearer/tap` — Homebrew refuses to load an untrusted tap formula.

joern-scan.why: code-property-graph SAST without a build (sast-joern) — the only C/C++ deep lane here
joern-scan.postInstall: run joernwork/bin/fix-local-joern.sh after EVERY brew upgrade — the local repairs live in the Cellar and an upgrade reverts them silently. bin/test/joern-local-repairs.test.mjs fails if they have.

rustfmt.why: Rust formatter the format-rust-rustfmt lane invokes through cargo fmt — SHIPPED WITH the rust toolchain as the rustfmt component, never installed on its own

cargo-clippy.why: Rust lint the lint-rust-clippy lane invokes — SHIPPED WITH the rust toolchain, never installed on its own

cargo.why: Rust toolchain; lint-rust-clippy runs through it

psalm.why: Psalm taint analysis (sast-php-psalm). PIN: composer global require vimeo/psalm:6.x-dev. The 6.16.1 RELEASE crashes on any codebase referencing the NAN constant (TLiteralFloat::getKey coerces it to string; PHP >= 8.5 raises); the fix is on the 6.x branch and unreleased -- verified 2026-09-02 by swapping the upstream file in and out of a pristine 6.16.1 install. Composer names that branch 6.x-dev, NOT dev-6.x. Do not use the brew phar: it additionally hits a PsalmPhar\Composer\InstalledVersions redeclare on any repo referencing that class (laravel, symfony, doctrine). PINNING A DEV BRANCH IS A REAL TRADE and was measured, not assumed: 6.x-dev fixes the NAN crash and introduces a php-parser AssertionError (assert(!isFirstClassCallable) in CallLike::getArgs) that aborts runs on a box with zend.assertions=1. The lane works around it by running psalm under zend.assertions=-1; upstream should still hear about it.

sobelow.why: Elixir/Phoenix SAST (sast-elixir-sobelow) — the ESCRIPT, not the mix task: the task runs inside the scanned project and needs its deps fetched
sobelow.postInstall: mix escript.install hex sobelow, then symlink ~/.mix/escripts/sobelow onto PATH — mix does not link escripts itself. Requires elixir.

composer.why: PHP dependency manager; required to install the phpcs-security-audit ruleset

phpcs-security-audit.why: THIRD-PARTY ruleset that gives sast-php-phpcs its security rules — PHP_CodeSniffer itself ships none, so phpcs alone is a style linter
phpcs-security-audit.postInstall: lands at ~/.composer/vendor/pheromone/phpcs-security-audit/Security, which is the path the lane defaults to (override with CW_PHPCS_SECURITY_STANDARD).

overwatch-layer-spine.why: The spine: the task ledger agent sessions file into, read by the panel Overwatch tab. NOT a scanner and NOT a binary on PATH — four hand-set pieces outside this repo, each checked read-only by admin/lib/spine-preconditions.mjs under the same ids as `steps`. DECLARATION ONLY: the panel shows which step is absent or misregistered and a human runs it; nothing in commitwork writes to ~/.claude.json or settings.json. The component is not published, so there is no url to fall back to and `steps` is the whole instruction. The registration MUST go in ~/.claude.json via `claude mcp add` — an mcpServers block in ~/.claude/settings.json is a key Claude Code never reads and was the first, silent, failure.

steps.mcp-registration: claude mcp add --scope user <name> -e SUBSTRATE_TASKS_DB=$HOME/.substrate/tasks.db -- node <checkout>/spine/mcp.mjs   # <name> is the server name the mcp__spine__* tools resolve to; then `claude mcp list` must show it ✔ Connected
steps.prompt-hook: in ~/.claude/settings.json hooks.UserPromptSubmit, a command hook that emits hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext instructing the session to use mcp__spine__* for task management (open_session first, list_plans, create_plan/create_task, update_task/set_status, close_session last)
steps.stop-hook: in ~/.claude/settings.json hooks.Stop, a command hook that emits systemMessage "spine: did the session record task progress? If so call mcp__spine__update_task and mcp__spine__set_status"
steps.hook-targets: every hook command in ~/.claude/settings.json must name a file that resolves. When one dangles, repoint the symlink at the surviving copy (`ln -sfn <new-target> ~/.claude/hooks/<name>`) or delete the hook entry — a hook whose target is gone stays declared and fires nothing. Same for ~/.claude/_functions, the @fn: primitive tree: it is one directory symlink and is resolved by session discipline, so a dangling tree reports nothing at all. D18 (commitwork evaluations/DECISIONS.md): 69 links from ~/.claude point into the vscode-skills checkout, so repoint before retiring it, never after.
steps.corpus-links: the 52 commands, 10 skills and the @fn: primitive tree under ~/.claude are symlinks into a checkout. Every one must resolve, and the @fn: tree is ONE directory link with no runtime resolver — if it breaks, every command silently loses its primitives and nothing errors. Repoint each link at the surviving checkout (spine under D18); never delete a checkout while any link still names it.
steps.launch-agent: macOS: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/net.portll.substrate.plist running node <checkout>/server/serve.mjs with RunAtLoad, then `launchctl load` it; the operator socket answers on 127.0.0.1:7980. Pair it with net.portll.substrate-spine-reap.plist so orphaned sessions are swept.

git.why: commit-provenance reads the object graph through `git log`; on macOS the Xcode command-line tools already provide it

gh.why: actions-health reads a repository's Actions history through gh api, with gh's own authentication

modelscan.why: OPTIONAL second witness for the model-artefacts lane: Protect AI's scanner over pickle/torch/keras artefacts. The lane runs its own zero-dependency opcode walker and records modelscan's verdict in summary.secondWitness when the binary is present; absence is stated, never a skip of the lane, so this is not in any check's requires.tools. Every release pins Requires-Python <3.13, so pipx must run a 3.10–3.12 interpreter (`pipx install --python python3.12 'modelscan[tensorflow,h5py]'`); without the extras it cannot open Keras or SavedModel files and reports a DEPENDENCY error per file rather than a verdict. Measured 2026-09-18 over the real canary artefacts: it agrees on the two Lambda layers and ReadFile, and does not flag EagerPyFunc.

cobolwork.why: COBOL, JCL and CICS security analysis and mainframe credential rules (sast-cobol-cobolwork, cobol-inventory, secrets-cobol-jcl lanes) - the only reader of mainframe source on the roster. Manual: the lanes run the release manifests/tool-pins.json pins, installed by bin/cobolwork-pin.mjs, never a cobolwork on PATH, and the repository is private
steps: the repository is private: `gh auth status` must show an account with read access to Portll/cobolwork
cobolwork.postInstall: --install downloads the asset manifests/tool-pins.json pins (gh release download, or --from <tgz>), refuses it unless its sha256, its lib/revision.json commit and its capabilities --json match the pin, and installs it under ~/.commitwork/tools/cobolwork/<version> (CW_TOOLS_ROOT moves it). Upgrading is --latest, which rewrites the pin, then a commit, then --install. CW_COBOLWORK_BIN runs another cobolwork in its place.

needs: read access to the private Portll/cobolwork repository, through the account `gh auth status` shows

socket.why: supply-chain / malicious-package detection (typosquats, install-script malware, obfuscation) — LISTED LAST because installing it is not enough to make it run

needs: an external Socket account (signup + login at socket.dev)
membership of an ORGANIZATION — `socket scan create` resolves an org slug and exits without one
an API token stored as SOCKET_CLI_API_TOKEN (see requires.secrets on supply-chain-socket)
an org role permitted to create scans; a read-only member cannot
requiresAccount.why: Every socket.json artifact in this repo's history is {ok:false, "Org name … (missing)"} — 0 pass / 40 token-skip / 25 noscan across 159 scan units on 2026-07-31. The binary installs fine and the check still never runs, so `✓ socket` in setup would otherwise read as coverage this fleet has never had.
requiresAccount.freeTier: Free plan covers unlimited private repos and developers but caps at 1,000 scans/month. MEASURED BY RUNNING IT 2026-08-10: a full fleet sweep costs 27 scans — the check applies only where package.json exists, 27 of 62 resolved repos — so nightly would be 810/month, INSIDE the tier. Two earlier figures were wrong in opposite directions: ~5,010 (counted every repo, wrong by 186×) and 23 (derived from a repo list that omitted area members). Both were arithmetic; 27 is observed. Quote the observed one. Socket is out of the `all` group regardless: 810/1000 is a 19% margin with no alarm on it, and an exhausted quota returns a refusal that lands as {ok:false}.
